- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND (literal, a string literal in executeGetRecordContext))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_ERROR (literal, 39 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b7bddeb91029a324cfe89c666fb62dd894fd730e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `47b38ecea244df88bc7c9eb53aa01ab1051a4bb1` — the merge of head `5f6f72fd82540c66a716be2a3a874bbd89e58bbd` into base `b7bddeb91029a324cfe89c666fb62dd894fd730e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 47b38ecea244df88bc7c9eb53aa01ab1051a4bb1 && git checkout 47b38ecea244df88bc7c9eb53aa01ab1051a4bb1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b7bddeb91029a324cfe89c666fb62dd894fd730e 5f6f72fd82540c66a716be2a3a874bbd89e58bbd && git checkout -B drift-repro b7bddeb91029a324cfe89c666fb62dd894fd730e && git merge --no-ff 5f6f72fd82540c66a716be2a3a874bbd89e58bbd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b7bddeb91029a324cfe89c666fb62dd894fd730e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b7bddeb91029a324cfe89c666fb62dd894fd730e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `64893151a8070e45d8532d5c1c8f4648a9309a45`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts + packages/services/service-record-context/src/body-outline.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/sentences.ts
Security-touching: yes

PR #37484, card #37233 (epic #36996). Read: the card body and its 7 comments (claim 7183671948, reports 7186736579 and 7187454759, claim amendment 7186766469), the PR body and its 2 comments, the net diff against `main` (12 files, +436/−44), the 74 check-runs on the head, ADR-0160 D3/D4 on `main`, and #37490. The security line reads `yes` because the executor hunk carries a disclosure rule (the one 404 answer that keeps `outlineFrom` from showing a body the caller's schema hides); no defect was found in it (see ④, Leaks).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Input accept-set widens by one optional member, nothing narrows — right.** `GetRecordContextInputSchema` gains `outlineFrom: z.number().int().min(0).optional()`. Every input `main` admits still parses and, with `outlineFrom` absent, `from` is 0 and the executor takes the path it took before. The generated `authorable-surface/ai.json` and `record-context-tools.mdx` agree with the zod file.
- **Output widens by one optional member — right.** `RecordContextBody.outlineNext: int, min 1, optional`. The floor holds in code: `next` is set only after at least one entry was admitted (a listable entry always fits an empty page: its length + 2 is at most 8,000), so `next` is greater than `from` and at least 1.
- **No note kind and no error code added — right.** `outline_truncated` keeps its kind and gets a new sentence; the two new refusals reuse `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` 404 and `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400.
- **Three behaviour changes on calls `main` already admits (no `outlineFrom`), all stated in the changeset — right, none a narrowing.** (a) The `outline_truncated` sentence is reworded, en and zh-Hans. (b) A cut outline's body now carries `outlineNext`. (c) N3: a heading whose entry alone passes the character bound is passed over, where `main` stopped the listing at it (or, when it came first, answered truncated text with no outline). Page 1 is otherwise the same set in the same order as `main`'s outline.
- **The mutual exclusion is not in the schema — right as declared, see N2.** The strict object admits `anchor` with `outlineFrom`; the executor refuses the pair. The field's `describe` says "Not with `anchor`".

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset: right. One optional input and one optional output member; nothing refused that was admitted.
- `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` minor: right by the gate's own reading. The authorable-surface ledger gains `GetRecordContextInput:outlineFrom` and `RecordContextBody:outlineNext`, and AGENTS.md step 3 gives an `added` kind at least minor. Precedent `.changeset/37140-…` graded spec minor for this tool's input.
- `@objectstack/service-record-context` patch: right. `boundedOutline` and its new `BoundedOutline` type are not exported from the package index (it exports the two constants only), so the package's public surface is unchanged; the behaviour change ships as patch under the repo rule (precedent `.changeset/37178-…`, patch for the cap itself). Both packages sit in the changesets `fixed` group, so they version together either way.
- Gate verdict, from the check-runs on the head: two `Check Changeset` runs exist. Run 139789254279 (workflow run 45784948113) started 08:39:01Z, completed 08:40:56Z, failure. Run 139789447261 (workflow run 45785004439) started 08:39:25Z, completed 08:41:17Z, success. The success is the newer by both timestamps, so the gate's standing answer on this head is success. The ordering is verified; that the failed run read the pre-edit PR body is the dev's account, consistent with the superseded `PR-body guards` run being cancelled at 08:39:25Z and its successor starting 08:39:28Z, but the failed run's log was not read here (its check-run output is empty). See N6.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question of report 7186736579 (which Metadata-protocol declaration stands): answered.** Option A, by claim amendment 7186766469; the changeset, PR body and newest `Check Changeset` agree.
- **Deviation: `packages/mcp/src/mcp-record-context-tools.test.ts` outside the first claim: acceptable.** One line, test only, no mcp source. The pin asserts the registration's exact input key list, so any input widening must move it or leave Test Core red. The claim amendment adds it to the file surface. It was amended after the PR opened, which is the honest order for a file the widening forced.
- **Deviation: ADR sentences carried by #37490, not this PR: right carrier.** `docs/adr/**` is Tier H; the card's Out-of-scope clause says the ADR text for a new input is a later amendment's, stated in the PR. #37490 is filed under #37233, blocked on this PR, and names both sentences (D4 input line, D3 "The body") plus the 404/400 behaviour. Until it lands, ADR-0160 D4's "Input, strict" line lists four members while the spec admits five; the card accepted that window. See N4 for the PR body's pointer.
- **Out-of-scope finding of the report (a heading too long to list has no issued anchor; in a flat body its section is unreachable through the tool), `carrier: none`: accepted as stated, not escalated.** The card allowed N3 "stated as is"; the note counts such headings and says their anchors are not given; it takes about 3,950 characters of heading text. The acceptance line "every section is reachable … by anchors it issued" holds for every heading that can be listed.
- **Report 7187454759 names its head `64893151a81`.** That is not a prefix of the head (`64893151a80…`). See N5.
- **Stale failed `Check Changeset` run left on the head:** see ② and N6.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Paging runs over the one body string the root read already returned. An outline page call repeats the whole pack read (fields, related lists), exactly as an `anchor` call does on `main`; that is the tool's existing shape, not a new cost class.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts` (hits)** against ADR-0160 D3/D4 and its first consumer, the executor.

- `outlineFrom` is declared in the input schema, strict object kept, integer of at least 0, projected to the tool's JSON Schema (spec test and the registration pin both read it). Holds.
- `outlineNext` min 1 matches the code (①). The note-kind jsdoc for `outline_truncated` matches the sentence. Holds.
- ADR-0160 D4 lists the input without `outlineFrom`. The card delegates the ADR text; #37490 carries it. Holds as a stated, carried gap.

**`body-outline.ts` — paging correctness.** Tried to break it; it holds.

- One order: `byLevel` sorts by level, then by body index, so the order is total and the same on every call for the same body. A page is the contiguous run of that order from `from` to `next`, minus unlistable headings. Runs of consecutive pages are disjoint and adjacent, so walking from 0 by `next` lists every listable heading exactly once, for flat and for mixed levels. No gap, no duplicate.
- Unlistable headings are skipped by `continue` before the cap test, at any position, including when the page is already full; `next` is only ever set at a listable heading.
- No livelock: `next` always points at a listable heading, which the next page admits first, so every page reached through `outlineNext` is non-empty; the executor emits `outlineNext` only on a non-empty page; and `next` is strictly greater than `from`.
- When only unlistable headings remain, `next` is absent and the sentence says no later page lists more.
- A passed-over heading stays readable by anchor: `sectionOf` resolves against every heading `headingsOf` gave, listed or not. The tool never issues that anchor, which the note states.
- Both bounds hold per page (entry cap; serialized characters with brackets and commas counted). No later step cuts the outline, so `outlineNext` cannot point past entries that were dropped.
- An `outlineFrom` that is not a boundary the tool issued gets the page starting there; harmless.

**`record-context-tools.ts` — contract and leaks.**

- 400 for `anchor` with `outlineFrom`: thrown in step 1, after parse and the locale read, before `readGuard`. It matches D4 "the arguments are validated" first, and the code and status are those of the parse refusal. The test pins `door.reads` empty.
- 404 for an outline page that does not start at `outlineFrom`: `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, the code an unresolved `anchor` gets, and D3's "one answer whatever the reason" extended to the new input. It is thrown in the body block, after the root gates, pack selection, the related children's gates and the reads, so no earlier answer changes: a caller the gates refuse gets the same 403/404 with or without `outlineFrom`.
- Leaks: for any `outlineFrom` above 0 the answer is the same code, status and sentence (it echoes only the number sent) for a page past the end, a body carried whole, a pack with no body, and a body the caller's projection withheld or dropped; the test compares the four refusals for equality. So `outlineFrom` cannot show that a pack has a body the caller's schema hides. `outlineNext` and the counts in the note are derived from a body the caller is reading. No finding.
- `outlineFrom: 0` is page 1, and on a body that is no outline it answers as a call without it. Consistent with the schema's floor.

**`sentences.ts` — sentence against code.**

- `outlineTruncated`, en and zh-Hans: listed, total, not-listed-on-this-page, the page order, the next `outlineFrom` or "no later page", and the unlistable count all match what `boundedOutline` returns. The clause a flat cut made false is gone. The two say the same thing. Holds.
- `outlineFromUnresolved` and `outlineFromWithAnchor`, en and zh-Hans: match the code. Hold.

S1 (should-fix) — On every outline page the executor still pushes the `body_outline` note, whose unchanged sentence reads "To read a section, call get_record_context again with the same arguments and that section's anchor" (zh-Hans: 用相同的参数和该节的 anchor). On a page reached with `outlineFrom` (page 2 onward), "the same arguments" include `outlineFrom`, and this PR makes `anchor` with `outlineFrom` a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. So the note this answer carries instructs a call the tool refuses, for every section listed past page 1, which is exactly the set of sections the card exists to make reachable. A model recovers from the refusal sentence, at the cost of a refused call. The acceptance pin does not see it: it reads each section with `{ ...CALL, anchor }`, never with the arguments of the page that issued the anchor. Fix in `sentences.ts`, en and zh-Hans (for example: with that section's anchor and without `outlineFrom`), and pin it by reading a section from page 2 the way the note says.

N1 (nit) — The cursor is a position in the current body's order. If the body is edited between two page calls, the walk can skip or repeat headings with no signal; anchors on each page are still current. "Each heading is on exactly one page" is true for one state of the body. The PR body says so; the spec `describe` and #37490's proposed D3 sentence do not. Carry the qualifier into #37490.

N2 (nit) — The `anchor`/`outlineFrom` exclusion lives in the executor and in `describe` prose only; the schema and its JSON Schema projection admit both. Acceptable for a strict object projected to JSON Schema, and the executor test pins the refusal. No spec test pins that the schema admits the pair, so the split is by convention.

N3 (nit) — Loose wording. Spec `outline`: "the pages run through every heading" and `outlineNext`: "when headings remain past this outline page" are both off by the too-long-to-list case (a later page must list one). The en sentence reads "1 of the headings are too long" when the count is 1.

N4 (nit) — The PR body names the ADR carrier as "the ADR-0160 amendment of #37202 or a later one"; the carrier is #37490. Prose face: point the PR body at #37490.

N5 (nit) — Delta report 7187454759 gives `"head": "64893151a81"`, which matches no commit; the head is `64893151a8070e45…`. The same report's gates line says `64893151a`, which does match. A record defect in the report, not in the tree.

N6 (nit) — The failed `Check Changeset` run 139789254279 stays on the head beside the newer success. It has no effect on the gate's standing answer; re-running that one job would clear the red mark for a human reader.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), which earns a delta review of its fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37233-outline-continuation`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `64893151a8070e45d8532d5c1c8f4648a9309a45`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5. Contract record 7187652688 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`) reads PASS: paging is correct, the contract holds, and nothing leaks. One should-fix, S1, closes in this PR before ACCEPT.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 12 files (+436/−44), `Fixes #37233`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. Changesets: spec minor, service-record-context patch. Not governed. All required contexts are green. The stale failed `Check Changeset` run (08:39:01Z) is superseded by the 08:39:25Z success.
2. **Premise**: pages are disjoint, adjacent runs of one total order, so every listable heading is listed exactly once. `outlineNext` is deterministic and strictly increasing, and no page can be empty. `outlineFrom` is in the strict input schema. The 404 is the same code, status and sentence for every not-listable case, thrown after the root gates. The 400 comes at step 1, before `readGuard`.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **S1.** The `body_outline` note on every page tells the caller to repeat "the same arguments" plus the section's anchor. On a page reached with `outlineFrom`, those arguments include `outlineFrom`, and `anchor` with `outlineFrom` is the 400 this PR adds. Fix the sentence in `sentences.ts`, in both en and zh-Hans, and pin a section read from page 2 that is done exactly as the note says.
   - The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**:
   - The mcp test-only registration pin is covered by the claim amendment.
   - Nits, fix in the same push if cheap:
     - N2: the exclusion is in the executor and `describe` only.
     - N3: wording gaps on too-long headings, and "1 of the headings are".
     - N4: the PR body should name #37490 as the ADR carrier.
     - N5: the head prefix in report 7187454759 is wrong.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: the ADR D3/D4 sentences go to #37490. N1 also goes there: the cursor is a position in the current body, so "exactly one page" holds per body state. #37490's D3 sentence should carry that qualifier.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Owed: S1 closed, a same-head delta PASS, and an **ACCEPT**. Then the area lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f6f72fd82540c66a716be2a3a874bbd89e58bbd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts + packages/services/service-record-context/src/body-outline.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/sentences.ts
Security-touching: yes

Delta round on PR #37484, card #37233 (epic #36996), and a whole record for this head. The earlier record is 7187652688 on `64893151a8070e45d8532d5c1c8f4648a9309a45`; the seat's REWORK is 7187667170. Read this round: the card's 8 comments (delta report 7189969133 among them), the PR body and its 4 comments, the two delta commits (`898c5e76ce`, `5f6f72fd82`: 5 files, +52/−13), the net diff against `main` (12 files, +477/−46), the 74 check-runs on this head, ADR-0160 D3/D4 on `main`, and #37490 with its 2 comments. The security line reads `yes` for the same reason as before: the executor hunk carries a disclosure rule (the one 404 answer that keeps `outlineFrom` from showing a body the caller's schema hides). The delta does not touch it and no defect was found in it.

The delta holds no merge of `main`. `main` is ahead of the branch's merge base (`a46efa8c6`) and has since moved three files of the service package (`index.ts`, `verify-citations.ts` and its test); none is in this diff, and the PR reads as mergeable clean.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Input accept-set widens by one optional member, nothing narrows — right, unchanged by the delta.** `GetRecordContextInputSchema` gains `outlineFrom: z.number().int().min(0).optional()`. With it absent the executor takes the path it took on `main`.
- **Output widens by one optional member — right, unchanged.** `RecordContextBody.outlineNext: int, min 1, optional`; the floor holds in code (`next` is set only after an entry was admitted, so it is above `from`).
- **No note kind and no error code added — right.** The two refusals reuse `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` 404 and `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400.
- **Behaviour changes on calls `main` already admits — right, none a narrowing.** (a) the `outline_truncated` sentence; (b) `outlineNext` on a cut outline; (c) a heading too long to list is passed over and counted; and, new in the delta, (d) the `body_outline` sentence is reworded on every outline answer, page 1 included (en and zh-Hans). It names the same call as before for a first-page caller, so no caller's working call changes. See N7 for the changeset's account of (d).
- **The delta's schema hunk is `describe` text only.** No accept-set moves; the regenerated `record-context-tools.mdx` rows agree with the zod file, and `authorable-surface/ai.json` is unchanged by the delta.
- **The `anchor` with `outlineFrom` exclusion stays the executor's — right as declared, and now pinned on both sides** (N2).

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/service-record-context` patch: right, and unchanged by the delta. The delta adds no key, no value and no export; the changeset file is not touched by it.
- Gate verdict, from the check-runs on this head: 74 runs, all completed, none failed (62 success, 12 skipped). `Check Changeset` ran twice, both success: 139823195841 started 09:45:49Z, and 139856513383 started 10:47:51Z after the PR body edit of 10:47:42Z. `PR-body guards` likewise twice, both success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Delta report 7189969133: no open question, no out-of-scope finding, `security_findings: none`.** Nothing to answer.
- **Its deviations: acceptable.** Unlocked single-file test runs while queued for the verify lock, with every reported reading re-taken under the lock at the final head; `gen:schema` and `gen:docs` run from source, then `check:generated` 14/14 under the lock.
